sections.title: Arizona AI regulatory context
sections.description: Key regulatory considerations for AI development in Arizona.

blocks.heading: Arizona Consumer Data Privacy Act
paragraphs: Arizona's consumer privacy legislation creates AI governance requirements for Tucson commercial applications.

blocks.heading: Arizona does not observe DST
paragraphs: Arizona (except Navajo Nation) does not observe Daylight Saving Time — ClickMasters operates on Arizona Standard Time (equivalent to Pacific DST in summer, Mountain Standard in winter) for Tucson clients.

sections.title: Tucson's technology growth trajectory
sections.description: Tucson's technology and AI market has been growing from its defense and university foundation.

blocks.heading: Raytheon's commercial technology spillover
paragraphs: Raytheon's enormous Tucson engineering workforce — 15,000+ employees working on some of the world's most technically demanding systems — has created a commercial technology ecosystem through spinouts, second-career entrepreneurs, and technology licensing that commercializes adjacent to Raytheon's core defense work.

blocks.heading: The University of Arizona's startup ecosystem
paragraphs: University of Arizona's Tech Parks Arizona is one of the US's most active university research park programs — commercializing research from UA's strong astronomy, optics, biosciences, and arid land research programs into startups that create private sector AI demand adjacent to the university's research programs.

blocks.heading: Bioscience cluster development
paragraphs: Tucson's BioScience Research Collaborative has been building a life science innovation cluster adjacent to the University of Arizona's campus — creating biotech and medical technology AI demand that adds to the healthcare and university technology AI market.

blocks.heading: Arizona's no-DST advantage
paragraphs: Arizona's year-round Mountain Standard Time (no daylight saving) creates specific timezone stability that some remote working arrangements and West Coast clients find valuable — engineers in Tucson are consistently 2–3 hours behind Eastern Time regardless of season.
